name: forced-colors
plain: True when Windows High Contrast or similar forces a palette.
meaning: Strong accessibility signal (low vision or migraine users). Mostly Windows contrast themes. A tiny share of users, hence very identifying for those who use it.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if Windows High Contrast or a similar mode is forcing your colors
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check whether forced colors are on
Change its design so text stays easy to see
Add the answer to a browser fingerprint
cannot: Tell why you turned it on, though it can hint at a vision need
Get an answer in Safari on Mac or iPhone
limits.reach_label: One yes or no, no prompt
limits.differs: Mostly a Windows setting. Safari on Mac and iPhone does not report it.

story.what_it_is: Tells a page that Windows High Contrast or a similar mode is forcing a color palette.

marketing.name: forced-colors media feature
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can detect forced colors modes and keep its content readable.

story.for_you: You may not know it is read. If you use High Contrast, the site can show clear borders and plain colors so buttons stay visible.
story.for_makers: Good makers use it to avoid unreadable pages for people with low vision or light sensitivity. It also reveals that a person may have a disability, which is private.

use_cases.example: A web app adds strong outlines to buttons and icons when high contrast mode is on so none disappear.
A browser word game swaps its color coded tiles for tiles with patterns or letters for high contrast users.
A banking site keeps charts readable by changing line colors and adding labels.
A document editor keeps selected text and comments visible when the palette is forced.
A fraud check treats forced colors as a normal real person signal and not as a bot.
A privacy minded team avoids logging the value because it can point to a disability.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
